Separation yields a nonzero nonnegative coefficient vector, normalizable to a probability on J. Expanding the derivative tests gives exactly the two inverse-ell marginals, with ell integrals one.

Both signs of every affine array are tight, so the dual inequality gives equal mass and first base moments. The finite nonnegative cone of tight anchored row normals is the correct dual sign for h_p−Σlambda_z h_z≥0. The flow decomposition is valid even when rows have self loops.

For visit mass m_p the identity mu+incoming=nu+outgoing follows coordinatewise from the Farkas representation. All target coefficients are positive, so the minimum stopping probability is positive and the visit system has a unique finite solution. Its stop mass is exactly nu, while initial injection has exactly mu.

Conditional mean of both z and ell is invariant across each anchored tight row and at absorbing self holds. Both functions are bounded on the finite base, so limits give both row equations and conditional Jensen gives convex order.

At any touching affine majorant the conditional base and ell means make expected nonnegative roof slack zero. If all nonidentity source relations are strict, rows must be identities; full target support then forces J=P and sigma=w. The same equal first moments place the tilted target barycenter in conv(J).

For the geometric consequence, vertices can only have identity rows. Full target support would then imply all sampled bases are vertices and hence pairwise parity-distinct by lattice completeness. The largest own centroid supplies at least gamma_d M/k(P) in every through-mark cap, with nonvertical buffering monotone and pure-base traces including the whole own fiber. This contradicts only the stated stronger beta<gamma_d/k(P).

The cited original finite separation, absorption, contact and nonvertex locators agree with the frozen claims. The proof is base-level; no conditional uniform fiber law, common physical stress or regular continued body menu is inferred.
